query: (Cathay MD) Build a model to organise/optimise routes and service so Overall Rating > 7.

per_column.name: review_sentiment
per_column.rationale: A bare positive/negative/neutral flag is fairly generic and largely redundant with existing Overall Rating and Recommended fields, giving limited new leverage for a route-optimisation model. Values are well grounded in the review text across all samples.

per_column.name: weakest_attribute
per_column.rationale: Identifying the weakest service dimension per review is directly actionable for prioritising service fixes. However groundedness is shaky: sample 1 (a story about being stranded, no food/reply) is labelled 'Value For Money' though the text points to staff/support; sample 4 explicitly complains about legroom/seat cramping yet is labelled 'Value For Money' rather than Seat Comfort. Several labels don't track the strongest textual signal, though it can also derive from the numeric sub-scores.

per_column.name: service_score_gap
per_column.rationale: A derived spread/gap across service sub-scores gives a genuine new axis to model consistency of experience. Values are plausibly computed from the existing numeric rating columns; not directly verifiable from text but not contradicted.

per_column.name: hub_route
per_column.rationale: Flagging Hong Kong hub routing is relevant for a Cathay route model, but the value is near-constant (714 vs 30), so it offers little discriminating power in practice. Values are well grounded in the Route field.

per_column.name: rating_vs_class_avg
per_column.rationale: Deviation of a review's Overall Rating from its class average is a strong analytical feature for spotting under/over-performing routes within comparable cabins. Computable from existing Class and Overall Rating columns; values are internally plausible though not textually checkable.

per_column.name: priority_action
per_column.rationale: A categorical action bucket (high_impact/on_track/borderline) directly serves the optimisation query by triaging where to act. Values largely follow sentiment/rating signals, though the derivation logic is opaque and the 'borderline_inconsistent' assignment in sample 5 is only loosely justified by the mixed text.

judge.rationale: Most added columns give genuine new axes (weakest_attribute, service_score_gap, rating_vs_class_avg, priority_action) for a route/service optimisation model, while review_sentiment and hub_route add less leverage due to redundancy and near-constancy respectively. Groundedness is generally acceptable and derivable from the text or existing numeric sub-scores, but weakest_attribute shows clear misreadings (legroom complaint and stranded-passenger story both tagged 'Value For Money'), which pulls the overall groundedness down.
